title: Coordinate differential basis, regular derivations and Taylor comparison
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $U$ a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n):U\to\mathbf A_k^n$ an etale morphism, $n\ge0$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space]. For every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq U$, the differentials $\mathrm dx_1,\ldots,\mathrm dx_n$ are an $A$-basis of $\Omega_{A/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. For every $A$-module $M$, evaluation on these coordinates is a bijection $\operatorname{Der}_k(A,M)\to M^n$, $D\mapsto(Dx_i)_i$. Consequently there are unique $k$-derivations $D_i:A\to A$ with $D_i(x_j)=\delta_{ij}$. They commute, are compatible with restriction to smaller affine opens, and induce derivations on the local rings. Thus iterated coordinate derivatives of regular functions are regular, and $\mathrm dc=\sum_iD_i(c)\,\mathrm dx_i$ for every $c\in A$. If $L/k$ is any field extension and $\tau:A\to L[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ is a $k$-algebra homomorphism with $\tau(x_i)=a_i+X_i$ for constants $a_i\in L$, then $\partial_{X_i}\tau(c)=\tau(D_ic)$ for every $c\in A$; the same identity holds on germs wherever $\tau$ extends, and for every iterated partial derivative. Formal power series and their partial derivatives mean [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. These statements include $n=0$.

proof.text: On an affine open V with section ring A, let theta:k[T_i] -> Gamma(A^n_k,O) be polynomial evaluation on the standard coordinates with the scalar map induced by the projection. AffineSpace.SpecIso_hom_appTop identifies GammaSpecIso.hom composed with theta with the global-section map of the affine-space spectrum isomorphism; hence theta is a ring isomorphism. The defining affine-local property of the given etale morphism gives that x.appLE(top,V):Gamma(A^n_k,O)->A is etale. Its composite with theta is etale and equals aeval of the restricted coordinate sections: check variables directly and constants using x.IsOver. This gives A its formally etale polynomial-algebra structure compatible with its canonical k-algebra structure. Base-change the polynomial Kahler basis through the formally etale differential isomorphism and reindex ULift(Fin n) by Fin n. The basis vectors are precisely d(x_i|V).

proof.text: For any A-module M, use the universal derivation equivalence Hom_A(Omega_A/k,M) = Der_k(A,M). Basis extensionality proves injectivity of coordinate evaluation; Basis.constr constructs a preimage of each tuple, proving surjectivity. Define D_i by composing d with the ith basis-coordinate linear map. Their values on x_j are delta_ij by the basis representation equations. The same evaluation injectivity proves uniqueness. The basis expansion of dc is the asserted sum because its ith coefficient is D_i(c). These constructions take values in A, so all finite iterates remain regular.

source.place: Tag 00RO; basis linear algebra and coordinate consequences written by the agent.

proof.text: Use Mathlib Derivation.commutator_apply for the Lie bracket of derivations. Its coordinate values vanish because D_i(x_l) and D_j(x_l) are zero or one. Coordinate evaluation injectivity identifies the commutator with zero, and evaluating at c gives D_i(D_j(c))=D_j(D_i(c)). This argument applies to any algebra whose coordinate differentials are a basis.

source.place: Tag 00RO; commutator cancellation and coordinate uniqueness written by the agent.

proof.text: For each point p choose an affine neighbourhood V. Its germ map A->O_U,p is localization at the corresponding prime. The canonical k-algebra structure on the stalk agrees with composition through A by germ_res. Localization is formally etale, so base-changing the affine differential basis through the formally etale differential isomorphism gives a stalk basis on the germs of the same global coordinate sections. Its ith dual coordinate derivation defines d_p,i; the preceding commutator argument proves its commutation. A general naturality lemma compares a derivation on B composed with a k-algebra map f:A->B with f composed with a derivation on A: both are derivations into B considered as an A-module via f, and equality on coordinates implies equality by the affine evaluation injectivity. Apply this first to restriction of sections, then to every germ map. The coordinate and scalar equalities follow from presheaf map composition and germ_res. This proves compatibility with every affine neighbourhood, independently of the affine open used to construct the stalk basis.

source.place: Tag 01HV for stalk localization; algebra.tex Tag 0H93 for differential base change; construction by dual bases written by the agent.

proof.text: For a k-algebra map tau:A->L[[X]], regard pderiv_L,i as a k-derivation by restriction of scalars. Compare its composite with tau with tau composed with D_i by the naturality/evaluation argument: on x_j the first is the derivative of C(a_j)+X_j, namely delta_ij, and the second is tau(delta_ij), which agrees. The same argument works on the stalk basis: any extending tau_p takes the global coordinate germs to C(a_j)+X_j by compatibility with tau, so the derivative identity follows directly on the entire stalk. Induction on List.foldr proves all iterated comparisons for sections and stalks; the empty list is reflexivity.

source.place: Tag 00RO; naturality, scalar restriction and word induction written by the agent.

proof.text: All arguments are uniform in n. For n=0 the empty basis has zero differential module, coordinate evaluation has the unique empty tuple, and differential expansion is the empty sum. For the empty affine open the ring and modules are zero, and all linear algebra remains valid. No characteristic assumption, factorial inverse, or field nontriviality of the section ring is used. The finite-type and quasi-compact hypotheses of the original statement are retained but not needed by this proof.
